From e0f3b803d74277677697bdf5b5e4c28766cfbc93 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Richard Weinberger <richard@nod.at>
Date: Tue, 26 Oct 2010 14:21:13 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] um: fix global timer issue when using CONFIG_NO_HZ

commit 482db6df1746c4fa7d64a2441d4cb2610249c679 upstream.

This fixes a issue which was introduced by fe2cc53e ("uml: track and make
up lost ticks").

timeval_to_ns() returns long long and not int.  Due to that UML's timer
did not work properlt and caused timer freezes.

Signed-off-by: Richard Weinberger <richard@nod.at>
Acked-by: Pekka Enberg <penberg@kernel.org>
Cc: Jeff Dike <jdike@addtoit.com>
Signed-off-by: Andrew Morton <akpm@linux-foundation.org>
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
Signed-off-by: Paul Gortmaker <paul.gortmaker@windriver.com>

diff --git a/arch/um/os-Linux/time.c b/arch/um/os-Linux/time.c
index dec5678fc17..6e3359d6a83 100644
--- a/arch/um/os-Linux/time.c
+++ b/arch/um/os-Linux/time.c
@@ -60,7 +60,7 @@ static inline long long timeval_to_ns(const struct timeval *tv)
 long long disable_timer(void)
 {
 	struct itimerval time = ((struct itimerval) { { 0, 0 }, { 0, 0 } });
-	int remain, max = UM_NSEC_PER_SEC / UM_HZ;
+	long long remain, max = UM_NSEC_PER_SEC / UM_HZ;
 
 	if (setitimer(ITIMER_VIRTUAL, &time, &time) < 0)
 		printk(UM_KERN_ERR "disable_timer - setitimer failed, "
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `arch/um/os-Linux/time.c`**
   - The type of the variable `remain` was changed from `int` to `long long`. This change ensures that the variable can properly hold larger values, which is necessary for the correct functioning of the timer in the UML (User Mode Linux) environment.
   - The change was made in the `disable_timer` function, where the variable `remain` is used.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modification in `time.c` addresses a bug related to the timer functionality in UML when the `CONFIG_NO_HZ` configuration is used. The original issue stemmed from the `timeval_to_ns()` function returning a `long long` value, which was not compatible with the `int` type of the `remain` variable. By changing `remain` to `long long`, the patch ensures that the timer can handle the values correctly, thus preventing timer freezes that were occurring due to this type mismatch. This fix is a direct response to the problem introduced by a previous commit (fe2cc53e) that aimed to improve tick tracking in UML.

Here is the commit message:
um: fix global timer issue when using CONFIG_NO_HZ

commit 482db6df1746c4fa7d64a2441d4cb2610249c679 upstream.

This fixes a issue which was introduced by fe2cc53e ("uml: track and make
up lost ticks").

timeval_to_ns() returns long long and not int.  Due to that UML's timer
did not work properlt and caused timer freezes.

Signed-off-by: Richard Weinberger <richard@nod.at>
Acked-by: Pekka Enberg <penberg@kernel.org>
Cc: Jeff Dike <jdike@addtoit.com>
Signed-off-by: Andrew Morton <akpm@linux-foundation.org>
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
Signed-off-by: Paul Gortmaker <paul.gortmaker@windriver.com>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by a type mismatch where the variable `remain` was declared as an `int`, while the function `timeval_to_ns()` returns a `long long`. This mismatch led to improper handling of timer values, resulting in timer freezes in the UML environment when using the `CONFIG_NO_HZ` configuration.

Here is the patch:
 
 long long disable_timer(void)
 {
 	struct itimerval time = ((struct itimerval) { { 0, 0 }, { 0, 0 } });
-	int remain, max = UM_NSEC_PER_SEC / UM_HZ;
+	long long remain, max = UM_NSEC_PER_SEC / UM_HZ;
 
 	if (setitimer(ITIMER_VIRTUAL, &time, &time) < 0)
 		printk(UM_KERN_ERR "disable_timer - setitimer failed, "
 		       "errno = %d\n", errno);
 
 	remain = timeval_to_ns(&time.it_value);
 	if (remain > max)
 		remain = max;
 
 	return remain;
 }

The variable `remain` is declared as an `int`, but the function `timeval_to_ns()` returns a `long long`. This type mismatch causes improper handling of timer values, leading to timer freezes in the UML environment when using the `CONFIG_NO_HZ` configuration.

The code statements that fix the bug are:

Reason:
Changing the declaration of `remain` from `int` to `long long` ensures that it can properly store the value returned by `timeval_to_ns()`, thus preventing the type mismatch and resolving the timer freeze issue.
